# 🤖 Multi-Agent Code Review Report

**PR**: #1687 — MPDX-9352, MPDX-9353, MPDX-9354 Customized login designs
**Branch**: `designs_for_customized_login` → `main`
**Agents**: 5 (Architecture, Data Integrity, Testing, UX, Standards)
**Review Mode**: Standard | **Risk Level**: HIGH (7/15) | **Consensus**: 95%

---

## 📊 Risk Assessment

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| **Risk Score** | 7/15 — HIGH |
| **Files Changed** | 51 (+749 -113) |
| **Required Reviewer** | ⚠️ Experienced developer or above |

**Risk Factors**: Shared components modified, new GraphQL operations, cross-cutting navigation changes, new access control logic

---

## 🚫 CRITICAL BLOCKERS (Severity 9-10) — Must fix before merge

### 1. Missing `id` field in `GetUserGroup.graphql` — Apollo cache broken

**Severity**: 9.7/10 (Consensus from ALL 5 agents)
**File**: `src/components/Shared/ConfirmUserGroupModal/GetUserGroup.graphql:1-5`

The query fetches `user { userType }` without an `id` field. CLAUDE.md requires: *"Always include `id` fields in queries/mutations for Apollo cache normalization."* Every other `user` query in the codebase (20+) includes `id`. Without it, Apollo cannot normalize the `User` object — cache updates from mutations won't propagate, causing stale/inconsistent data.

**Fix**:
```graphql
query GetUserGroup {
  user {
    id
    userType
  }
}
```
Then run `yarn gql`.

---

### 2. Conditional Hook Calls in `MultiPageMenu.tsx` — React Rules violation

**Severity**: 10/10 (Architecture agent)
**File**: `src/components/Shared/MultiPageLayout/MultiPageMenu/MultiPageMenu.tsx:102-107`

Hooks are called inside a ternary expression:
```typescript
const navItems =
    navType === NavTypeEnum.Reports
      ? useReportNavItems()
      : navType === NavTypeEnum.HrTools
        ? useHrToolsNavItems()
        : useSettingsNavItems();
```
This violates React's Rules of Hooks. If `navType` changes between renders, different hooks are called in the same slot, corrupting React's internal state.

**Fix**: Call all hooks unconditionally:
```typescript
const reportNavItems = useReportNavItems();
const hrToolsNavItems = useHrToolsNavItems();
const settingsNavItems = useSettingsNavItems();
const navItems =
    navType === NavTypeEnum.Reports
      ? reportNavItems
      : navType === NavTypeEnum.HrTools
        ? hrToolsNavItems
        : settingsNavItems;
```

> **Note**: This extends a pre-existing pattern, but adding `useHrToolsNavItems` makes it worse.

---

## 🔴 HIGH PRIORITY (Severity 7-8) — Should fix before merge

### 3. GraphQL operation name starts with "Get"

**Severity**: 7.0/10 | **File**: `GetUserGroup.graphql:1`

CLAUDE.md: *"Use descriptive names, not starting with 'Get' or 'Load'."* Rename to `UserGroup`.

---

### 4. Fire-and-forget mutations — no error handling

**Severity**: 7.6/10 (4 agents) | **File**: `ConfirmUserGroupModal.tsx:33-53`

Both `handleRequestChange` and `handleCustomConfirm` call `updateUserOption()` without `await`, `.catch()`, or result checking. If the mutation fails, the user sees the modal close and believes their preference was saved. `handleRequestChange` also fires `window.location.href = 'mailto:...'` regardless of success.

**Fix**: `await` the mutation, handle errors with a snackbar, only close on success.

---

### 5. Non-localized strings in `getUserType.ts`

**Severity**: 7.0/10 (4 agents) | **File**: `getUserType.ts:5-12`

Hardcoded English strings (`'Cru US Staff'`, `'Cru Global Staff'`, `'Non Cru User'`, `'Unknown'`) displayed in the modal. All user-visible text must use `t()`.

---

## ⚠️ IMPORTANT ISSUES (Severity 6-7)

### 6. Dashboard `useEffect` logic — PENDING check is dead code

**Severity**: 6.8/10 (ALL 5 agents) | **File**: `Dashboard.tsx:42`

```typescript
if (!loading && !userGroup && userGroup !== 'PENDING') {
```
When `userGroup` is `'PENDING'`, `!userGroup` is already `false` — the `!== 'PENDING'` check is never reached. Works by accident but misleading. Simplify to `!loading && !userGroup`.

---

### 7.

The `FormControl` has `component="fieldset"` but there is no `<FormLabel component="legend">`. The question text is in a standalone `<Typography>` not programmatically associated with the group. Screen readers will not announce the group's purpose.

[Nice-to-have] Consider using `it.each` for repetitive pending status tests

Several test files have near-identical test cases repeated for each pending status (e.g., `EligibleDisplay.test.tsx:85-127`, `CurrentRequest.test.tsx:173-222`, `AdditionalSalaryRequest.test.tsx:184-258`, `getDotColor.test.ts:10-42`). Using `it.each` would reduce ~60 lines of duplication:

```ts
it.each([
  AsrStatusEnum.Pending,
  AsrStatusEnum.PendingDivisionHeadApproval,
  AsrStatusEnum.PendingVpApproval,
  AsrStatusEnum.PendingManagementApproval,
  AsrStatusEnum.PendingBoardApproval,
])('displays pending message for %s', async (status) => { ... });
```

Purely a style suggestion — current approach is perfectly functional.

---

[Nice-to-have] Consider an `isApproved` helper alongside `isPending`

In `CurrentRequest.tsx:124-126`, the `ApprovedNotPaid || ApprovedAndPaid` check appears inline and is also repeated in `getDotColor.ts` / `getDotVariant.ts`. If more approved statuses are added in the future, an `isApproved` derived boolean in the context would be consistent with the `isPending` pattern.

---

Overall this PR looks great — clean approach centralizing `isPending` in the context, thorough test coverage for all new statuses, and well-scoped changes. 👍

payload.title: MPDX-9323 Stop rounding to zero in MHA/ASR

payload.author: kegrimes
payload.body:
## 🤖 Code Review — MPDX-9323 Stop rounding to zero in MHA/ASR

**Risk**: MEDIUM (4/10) | **Reviewer Level**: Mid-level/Senior | **Files**: 10 | **Lines**: +96 -31

---

### High Confidence Issues

**[Must-fix] Inconsistent test assertions — two tests still expect values without `.00`**
📍 `Deduction.test.tsx:386` and `Deduction.test.tsx:394`

The "updates total when traditional403bContribution changes" test asserts `'$2,500'` and the "updates total when roth403bContribution changes" test asserts `'$0'`. Every other test was updated to include `.00`. These will likely fail since `currencyFormat` with `showTrailingZeros: true` produces `$2,500.00` and `$0.00`.

Fix: `'$2,500'` → `'$2,500.00'` and `'$0'` → `'$0.00'`

---

**[Must-fix] Missing `locale` in `useSaveField` callback dependency array**
📍 `useSaveField.ts:79-86`

The `saveField` callback uses `locale` (via `amountFormat(overallAmount, locale)` at line 40), but `locale` is not in the `useCallback` dependency array. If locale changes during a session, the callback would use a stale value.

Fix: Add `locale` to the dependency array.

---

**[Must-fix] `amountFormat` returns empty string for zero values**
📍 `useSaveField.ts:40` → `intlFormat.ts:58-61`

`amountFormat` returns `''` when value is falsy, including `0`. If `overallAmount` computes to `0`, the mutation sends an empty string as `overallAmount` instead of `'0'` or `0`.

Fix: Handle the zero case, e.g.:
```ts
const roundedOverallAmount = overallAmount === 0 ? '0' : amountFormat(overallAmount, locale);
```

---

**[Nice-to-have] `amountFormat` uses `trailingZeroDisplay: 'stripIfInteger'`**
📍 `useSaveField.ts:40`

Integer values like `424` format as `"424"` while `424.44` becomes `"424.44"`. This creates inconsistent string formats sent to the server. Worth verifying the server handles both.

---

### Medium Confidence Issues

**[Nice-to-have] `isDecimal` allows empty string and lone dot**
📍 `formatHelper.ts:12-14`

The regex `/^\d*\.?\d*$/` matches `""` and `"."`. Empty string is handled by an earlier check, but `"."` would pass `isDecimal`, call `Number(".")` → `NaN`, and set `NaN` in form state.

Fix: Tighten regex to require at least one digit:
```ts
export const isDecimal = (s: string) => {
  return /^\d+\.?\d*$|^\d*\.\d+$/.test(s);
};
```

---

**[Nice-to-have] Removing `Math.round` may produce floating-point precision artifacts**
📍 `useSalaryCalculations.ts:62-63`

`total * traditional403bPercentage` can produce artifacts like `399.96000000000004`. Display is fine since `currencyFormat` rounds, but raw numbers propagated through the component tree carry precision noise.

---

### Low Confidence Suggestions

**[Nice-to-have] Consider `toFixed(2)` instead of `amountFormat` for server-bound data**
📍 `useSaveField.ts:40`

Using a locale-aware display formatter for server submission conflates display and data formatting. In some locales, `Intl.NumberFormat` uses different decimal separators (e.g., `424,44`). If the server expects standard decimal format, `overallAmount.toFixed(2)` would be safer.

---

### Testing Suggestions

- `isDecimal` in `formatHelper.ts` has no dedicated unit tests. Consider testing edge cases: `""`, `"."`, `"123"`, `"12.34"`, `"12.34.56"`, `"abc"`, `"-5"`.
- Consider a test for floating-point edge cases in `useSalaryCalculations` (e.g., percentage `0.07` on `3333`).

---

_🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

payload.body:
# 🤖 Multi-Agent Code Review Report

**PR #1639**: MPDX-9273: Add spouse request flows for ASR and MHA
**Agents**: 6 specialized reviewers (Architecture, Data Integrity, Testing, UX, Financial, Standards) with 2 debate rounds
**Review Mode**: Standard (smart agent selection)

---

## 📊 Risk Assessment

**Risk Score**: 13 — **CRITICAL**
**Files Changed**: 16 (+489 -100 lines)

**Risk Factors**:
- `src/lib/apollo/cache.ts` modified (55 dependents)
- `AdditionalSalaryRequestContext.tsx` modified (27 dependents)
- `.graphql` schema changed
- 500+ lines changed

**Required Reviewer**: Senior developer should review

---

## ⚠️ Important Issues (Should fix before merge)

### 1. Missing `isSpouse=true` test coverage in SpouseComponent (8/10)
**Consensus**: 5 of 6 agents flagged

`SpouseComponent` has critical conditional logic (lines 23-28) that swaps which calculations are used based on `isSpouse`. The link text also changes. **None of this is tested** — all 6 test cases use `isSpouse: false`.

Suggested tests:
```tsx
it('shows "Switch back to" text when isSpouse is true', ...);
it('uses userCalculations for remaining salary when isSpouse is true', ...);
it('generates correct link URL when isSpouse is true (no query param)', ...);
```

### 2. Duplicated spouse link logic across 3 components (7.5/10)
**Consensus**: All 6 agents flagged

Identical logic is copy-pasted in `SpouseComponent.tsx`, `InProgressDisplay.tsx`, and `StepList.tsx`:
- Same link text computation
- Same URL construction

**Recommendation**: Extract into a shared `useSpouseLink()` hook.

### 3. Missing `isSpouse=true` tests in InProgressDisplay and StepList (7/10)
**Consensus**: 4 of 6 agents flagged

Neither component tests the `isSpouse=true` path — "Switch back to" text, link URL without `?isSpouse=true`, and StepList spouse link rendering are all unverified.

### 4. "Switch back to" link text is ambiguous (7/10)
When `isSpouse=true`, "Switch back to {{name}}" doesn't clearly communicate the action. Consider "View {{name}}'s request" or similar.

---

## 💡 Medium Priority (Consider addressing)

- **(7/10)** Full page navigation for spouse switching — Uses MUI `<Link href>` instead of `next/link`, causing full page reload
- **(6/10)** Hardcoded past-due date "9/25/2025" in StepList — **Pre-existing**, not introduced by this PR, but exposed to more users. Recommend follow-up ticket.
- **(6/10)** `isSpouse: isSpouse || undefined` coercion asymmetry between query and mutation
- **(5/10)** Backend contract for `calculations` orientation should be documented with a code comment
- **(5/10)** Inconsistent nullish coalescing (`||` vs `??`) in `useFormUserInfo.ts`

---

## ✅ Positive Findings

- Apollo cache `keyArgs: ['isSpouse']` correctly prevents cache collision
- Context-level user/spouse swap is well-implemented with good test coverage
- 403b percentage swap logic is tested and correct
- All user-visible text properly localized with `t()`
- Gender-neutral language improvement ("her" → "their")
- Named exports, `id` fields in GraphQL, no security issues, no `any` types

---

## 📝 Debate Summary

The Data Integrity Agent initially flagged two **CRITICAL (10/10)** findings about `useSalaryCalculations` and `useFormUserInfo` not being `isSpouse`-aware. After cross-examination by Architecture, Testing, Financial, and Standards agents, both findings were **conceded and downgraded to 5/10 and 4/10** respectively. The context-level swap and backend `isSpouse` query parameterization handle the data orientation correctly. The residual concern is an implicit backend contract that should be documented.

---

## 🎯 Recommended Next Steps

**Should fix before merge:**
- [ ] Add `isSpouse=true` test cases to `SpouseComponent.test.tsx`
- [ ] Extract shared spouse link logic into a hook
- [ ] Add `isSpouse=true` test coverage to `InProgressDisplay` and `StepList`

**Consider addressing:**
- [ ] Clarify "Switch back to" link text
- [ ] Use `next/link` for SPA navigation
- [ ] Add code c
